title: Things to Do in Seattle: Three Stops Between the Market and the Water
description: Explore Pike Place MarketFront, Pier 62 and Olympic Sculpture Park on a Seattle waterfront outing with practical visiting tips.
body:
Looking for things to do in Seattle around Pike Place Market and the waterfront? Give MarketFront, Pier 62 and Olympic Sculpture Park an outing of their own. They offer three different public settings between the market, the bay and outdoor art.

The plan works best when you leave time to enjoy the connections as well as the stops. You do not need a ferry departure, a performance or a cloudless view of the mountains to make the afternoon worthwhile.

1. Start at Pike Place MarketFront

On the Western Avenue side of Pike Place Market, MarketFront adds public space overlooking the waterfront. The market’s MarketFront introduction explains this part of the market and its location.

Spend some time on the open public deck before deciding where to shop or eat. It is a chance to appreciate the market as part of the wider city, rather than only as a list of counters to visit. Give the view enough time to become more than a quick photo.

Plan the stop: Follow current public-access signs and keep business entrances clear. The deck visit does not require a purchase. Individual shops and restaurants have their own hours, so plan any food stop separately.

2. Move toward the water at Pier 62

Pier 62 is a public waterfront space near the foot of Pine Street. Friends of Waterfront Park’s visitor page lists current hours and explains its role as a place for both everyday visits and community programming.

Enjoy the open main pier as it is when you arrive. An event can be a bonus, but the water and city setting are enough to spend time with on their own. Let this be a place where the outing slows down before you continue north.

Plan the stop: Use the main public pier and follow event or weather restrictions. Floating-dock access is separate and unnecessary for this suggestion. Check current waterfront visitor updates if lifts, ramps or route changes affect your plans.

3. Look at art in Olympic Sculpture Park

At 2901 Western Avenue, Olympic Sculpture Park brings large-scale works into a waterfront landscape. The Seattle Art Museum’s park guide lists free admission, hours and visitor rules.

Choose an open path and spend time with the art that catches your attention. You do not need to see every work or agree with your companion about what it means. The relationship between sculpture and landscape is part of the experience.

Plan the stop: Do not touch or climb sculptures, and remain on paths and walkways. The museum asks visitors to walk bikes and scooters through the park. Check seasonal closing times rather than assuming the park stays open after dark.

Plan for Seattle’s changing levels and weather

Start at MarketFront, use the currently open connection to the waterfront, visit Pier 62, then continue north toward Olympic Sculpture Park. Allow about three hours as a flexible planning budget with pauses.

Seattle’s changes in level make the choice of connection important. Check current waterfront visitor updates before heading down from the market. The public-space stops do not require attraction tickets; meals, transport and optional attractions are separate. Bring a layer and read our Seattle visitor guide for more local context.
